title: Why is it called a ‘Large’?
sub: Small peg, large peg, Patiala peg.

cards.head: We pour pegs, not shots.
cards.body: Spirits here are traditionally measured by the peg.

cards.head: A small peg.
cards.body: Also called a ‘chota’ peg. About one fluid ounce.

cards.head: A large peg. ‘Ek large.’
cards.body: Ask for just ‘a peg’ and this is usually the one people mean.

cards.head: The peg measure.
cards.body: A double-ended steel cup: 30 ml on one side, 60 ml on the other.

cards.head: Patiala peg.
cards.body: Legend says Maharaja Bhupinder Singh of Patiala (ruled 1900–1938) served giant pegs to a visiting team the night before a match.

cards.head: One large. Slowly.
cards.body: Water between every peg, food on the table, and nobody drives.

caption:
Why is it called a “Large”? 🥃 Small peg, large peg and the Patiala peg, explained.

In India, spirits are traditionally measured in pegs, not shots.
Small (chota) peg: 30 ml.
Large (bada) peg: 60 ml. Ask for just “a peg” and this is usually the one people mean.
Bars measure it with a double-ended peg measure: 30 ml on one side, 60 ml on the other.
The Patiala peg (about 120 ml) is a legend: Maharaja Bhupinder Singh of Patiala is said to have served giant pegs to a visiting team the night before a match.

Chota or large: which do you order? Comment below 👇 and send this to the friend who always says “ek large”.

Water between every peg. Drink slow. Never drink and drive. 18+
